ins.strong: Uses multiple threads for managing heap space

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Can specify maximum garbage collection threads and pause time, throughput, and
footprint - heap size

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Freezes all application threads when it runs.
It's not good idea to use it with multi-threaded apps, like server environments

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Default GC of the JVM from Java 5 until Java 8
and is sometimes called Throughput Collectors.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Numbers of garbage collector threads
JVM option:
XX:ParallelGCThreads=NUMBER_OF_THREADS

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Maximum pause time goal - a hint to the GC that pause times of NUMBER_OR_MILLISECONDS milliseconds or less are desired
JVM option:
XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=NUMBER_OR_MILLISECONDS

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Time spent doing garbage collection versus the time spent outside of garbage collection is called the maximum throughput target
JVM option:
XX:GCTimeRatio=MAXIMUM_THROUGHPUT

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Maximum heap footprint - the amount of heap memory that a program requires while running
JVM option:
XmxAMOUNT_OF_HEAP_MEMORY
